### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_settings`

Core global settings for the entire AI Shopping Mall system. Stores
key-value configuration data (system environment parameters, feature
flags, legal, policy constraints, etc) that impact cross-domain
functionality. Critical for environment-wide policy propagation and
system-level toggles. Each configuration entry is atomic and
version-auditable.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `conf_key`
  > Unique key identifying the system configuration parameter (e.g.,
  > 'maintenance_mode', 'default_locale').
- `conf_value`
  > The effective value of the system configuration parameter. Content, type,
  > and semantics are determined by conf_key.
- `description`: Optional business/admin description of the setting's meaning or scope.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of this configuration entry.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp of this entry.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (if entry was deleted logically; otherwise null).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels`

Represents a business channel in the AI Shopping Mall system (e.g.,
separate brand, marketplace, partner-tenant, B2B space). Channels
partition the marketplace, enabling isolated business/marketing policies
and operations. Key relationships: may host multiple sections and
categories (via mapping). Includes branding, access, and activation
fields.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `created_by_admin_id`
  > Administrator who created or manages this channel. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id}.
- `code`
  > Unique business code for channel reference, external integration, and
  > business logic (e.g., 'KOR_BRAND01').
- `name`: Channel's official display name.
- `description`: Detailed business purpose or scope for this channel.
- `logo_url`: Branding/logo file URI.
- `active`: Whether the channel is currently active (business logic switch).
- `created_at`: Channel creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (if entry was deleted logically; otherwise null).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_sections`

Sections are curated areas within a channel to organize products/events
(e.g., best sellers, promotions). Each section belongs to a channel.
Business can define as many dynamic sections as needed. Includes display
order and status/visibility options.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_id`: Linked business channel's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels).
- `created_by_admin_id`
  > Admin who created this section. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id}.
- `code`
  > Unique identifier for section within channel (e.g., 'best', 'main',
  > 'promotion').
- `name`: Section's display name.
- `description`: Detailed context for this section's curation purpose.
- `display_order`: Explicit order for sorting/display of this section within the channel.
- `visible`
  > Visibility toggle for the section (e.g., is this section shown to users
  > currently).
- `created_at`: Section creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (if deleted logically).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories`

Product/category taxonomy tree (multi-level). Each row is a single
category that can be nested by parent_id (hierarchical). Enables
fine-grained classification for products and curation. Used for search,
filtering, menu, recommendation, and reporting. Soft deletes allow
preserving taxonomy for historical/business reference.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`
  > Optional parent category for hierarchy. Self-references {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories.id}.
- `created_by_admin_id`
  > Admin who created this category. References {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id}.
- `code`: Unique category code (internal taxonomical ID).
- `name`: Display name for this category (shown to users/business).
- `description`: Detailed context or purpose of this category.
- `display_order`: Ordering index for UI rendering.
- `visible`: Whether the category is shown to users (UI toggle).
- `created_at`: Category creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (if logically deleted).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_channel_category_map`

Junction table associating channels and categories for dynamic curation.
Enables a many-to-many relationship: one channel can promote many
categories, one category can appear in many channels. Composite unique to
prevent duplication. Used for section/category navigation, AI curation,
analytics, and partitioned UIs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `channel_id`: Referenced channel [shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels).
- `category_id`: Referenced category [shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories).
- `created_at`: Mapping creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (null if active).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments`

Centralized metadata for all files or attachments used system-wide
(images, docs, certificates, legal, product assets, etc). Manages the
business-context origin of the file, owner, access control, security
context, and expiry. Structured for true polymorphic ownership: supports
reference to any business entity type via owner_id and owner_type. This
design enables attachments to be linked to admins, products, customers,
sellers, orders, etc., supporting long-term scalability, compliance and
cross-domain file use. Polymorphism is managed at the application and
convention layer; owner_type must be present and valid for each
attachment. Critical for file compliance, auditing, and tracking linked
business data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `owner_id`
  > UUID of the owning entity for the attachment; compatible with any
  > business object's PK (admin, product, customer, order, etc.). Interpreted
  > in conjunction with owner_type for context.
- `owner_type`
  > String discriminator specifying business type/classification of owner
  > (e.g., 'admin', 'seller', 'product', 'customer', 'order', etc.). Used for
  > context routing and polymorphic relations. Must match one of the
  > supported domain types documented in system.
- `file_name`: Original file name as uploaded.
- `file_size`: File size in bytes.
- `mime_type`: MIME type (content type) for file; used for validation and download.
- `storage_uri`: Physical storage URI for file data (object storage, CDN URI, local, etc).
- `hash_sha256`: SHA-256 checksum hash for file integrity and deduplication.
- `uploaded_at`: Timestamp of actual upload/ingest of this file into the system.
- `expire_at`
  > Expiration timestamp of this file; after which file should be deleted or
  > is invalid. Null if indefinite/never expires.
- `created_at`: Attachment record creation time (audit field).
- `updated_at`: Record last update timestamp (audit field).
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp (for logical deletes, otherwise null).
- `description`
  > Optional business/admin description about the file content, usage
  > purpose, or any compliance detail.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachment_logs`

Attachment/file event logs (upload, download, deletion, access) for
auditing and forensic operations. Polymorphic support for owner; records
WHAT (event/action type), WHEN, WHERE (ip), and context about every file
operation. Ensures traceability for file access, regulatory compliance,
and troubleshooting. FK to attachments (polymorphic), logs operator_admin
as actor when available.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `attachment_id`: Attachment file [shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_attachments).
- `event_type`
  > Type of file event (e.g., 'upload', 'download', 'delete', 'access',
  > 'expire', etc.).
- `event_context`
  > Business or technical context of the event. Optional log details for
  > troubleshooting or tracing.
- `ip_address`
  > IP address from which the attachment event happened (for audit/security
  > purposes).
- `operated_by_admin_id`
  > Admin/operator who performed the action (when relevant). References admin
  > ID, nullable for automated/system events or non-admin actions.
- `event_at`: Precise timestamp when the event occurred.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers`

Customer account data for the shoppingMallAiBackend system. Records all
registered end users including personal/contact details, login
credentials, account status, channel for signup, and profile setup. This
model is the master entity for customer identity including relationship
to addresses, external OAuth links, and customer histories. Does not
contain calculated or denormalized data.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Customer's unique business email address used for authentication and
  > notifications.
- `password_hash`: Hashed value of the customer's login password.
- `name`: Full name of the customer for verification and profile display.
- `nickname`
  > Customer's unique display nickname. Required for social, review, and
  > community activities.
- `phone`: Customer's mobile phone number (used for verification and contact).
- `profile_image_uri`: URI for customer's profile image. Used for display in UI.
- `status`
  > Account status (active, locked, dormant, withdrawn, etc.).
  > Business-driven state for access and communications.
- `email_verified`: Indicates whether the customer's email is verified.
- `phone_verified`: Indicates whether the customer's phone is verified.
- `joined_at`: Timestamp of initial customer registration.
- `last_login_at`: Most recent login datetime for the customer account.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for record (for auditing).
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last update to customer data.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp of soft deletion (if any, null when not deleted).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_addresses`

Addresses owned and managed by customers. Stores multiple shipping or
billing addresses per customer, including main/default flag. References
parent customer entity. Separate model ensures that address history,
verification events, and clustering are possible without denormalization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
- `alias`
  > User-defined alias or description (e.g., Home, Work, Parent's house) for
  > quick selection.
- `receiver_name`: Recipient's name for delivery purposes (may differ from account name).
- `receiver_phone`: Recipient's phone number.
- `postal_code`: Postal code for address verification and delivery routing.
- `address_line1`: Primary street address information.
- `address_line2`: Secondary (optional) address info (unit, building, floor).
- `city`: City or locality used for logistics and region assignment.
- `state`: State or province within the country.
- `country`: Country (ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code preferred).
- `is_primary`
  > Indicates if this address is marked as the customer's primary default
  > address.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the address record.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification for address data.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if address is active.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_external_links`

External OAuth/OpenID/social account links attached to customer accounts
for login and profile federation. One record per (customer, provider,
external ID) combination. Includes metadata for identity provider.
Enables SSO/integration without denormalizing into customer profile.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
- `provider`: External auth provider (e.g., google, kakao, naver, apple, etc.).
- `external_id`: External system's user identifier (sub, sns ID, etc).
- `linked_at`: Datetime of first link (binding) with customer account.
- `last_auth_at`: Most recent successful authentication event at provider, if known.
- `metadata_json`
  > Opaque JSON data with provider-specific profile payload (trusted identity
  > assertion, profile syncs, metadata, etc).
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of this external link record.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for external link info.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp. Null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_histories`

Snapshot-based record of significant lifecycle events or changes to a
customer account. Enables audit trails, compliance histories, and
rollback/recovery for customer state including registration,
verification, profile changes, status shifts (dormant/withdrawn), etc.
Always references customer entity and records event type, old/new values,
and trigger context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
- `event_type`
  > Type of lifecycle event (created, updated, verified, password_changed,
  > locked, withdrawn, etc).
- `old_value_json`: JSON snapshot of previous state/fields (before change).
- `new_value_json`: JSON snapshot of new state/fields (after change).
- `triggered_by`: Trigger source (user, system, admin, external).
- `meta_json`
  > Additional contextual metadata about the event (IP address, device,
  > channel, error codes etc.).
- `occurred_at`: Datetime the history event occurred.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers`

Seller business accounts. Core info for merchants/partners/brands
operating as vendors in the shoppingMallAiBackend. Differentiated from
customers/admins. Contains business identity, core profile, contact and
verification status fields. Relates to business verification, onboarding
workflow, and audit histories for compliance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`
  > Seller's unique business email for login, communication, and
  > notifications.
- `password_hash`: Hashed login password for seller account.
- `company_name`: Registered company/entity name as per legal documentation.
- `business_number`: National or regional business registration number (e.g., KR 10-digit).
- `representative_name`: Name of business owner or representative for contracts and compliance.
- `address`: Business's main office address for legal/certification use.
- `phone`: Primary business contact phone.
- `status`: Current seller account status (pending, active, suspended, withdrawn).
- `email_verified`: Indicates whether seller's email is verified.
- `joined_at`: Datetime of seller's registration.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for seller record.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last seller info update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_business_verifications`

Business registration and documentation verification records for sellers.
One record per verification step or artifact (e.g., business certificate,
bankbook, ID proof), including status, approval, and reviewer/admin info.
Enables compliance with ecommerce/regulatory laws. Always references
seller entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Belonged seller's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers).
- `document_type`
  > Type of submitted document (business_license, identity_card, bankbook,
  > etc).
- `document_file_uri`: URI to the uploaded file storage for this document.
- `verification_status`
  > Verification process status (pending, approved, rejected,
  > reupload_required, etc).
- `reviewed_by`
  > Reviewer/admin name or identifier who performed the audit, null if
  > pending/automated.
- `reviewed_at`: Datetime when document was reviewed and approved/rejected.
- `note`: Admin or reviewer note about this verification event.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of record creation.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_onboardings`

Tracks onboarding workflow status and history for each seller. Includes
milestone dates for each onboarding stage, approvals, issues, admin
actions, and notes. Comprehensive reference for compliance, readiness,
and audit. Linked to main seller record. Only contains raw event data, no
denormalized calculations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Belonged seller's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers).
- `step_code`
  > Onboarding stage code or type (application, document_upload, ai_review,
  > admin_review, activated, onboarding_failed, etc.).
- `step_status`
  > Current status/final decision for this onboarding step (pending,
  > completed, failed, need_revision, etc.).
- `approved_by`
  > Admin who approved/passed the onboarding stage. Nullable if not reviewed
  > by human.
- `occurred_at`: Datetime of event or status change for this onboarding step.
- `note`: Admin/system note about this onboarding step/event.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for onboarding event record.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_seller_histories`

Audit/snapshot history of major seller account events or state changes.
Tracks updated profile info, password resets, account status changes,
onboarding completions, suspensions, withdrawal, etc. Provides
comprehensive historical trail for compliance and support. Always
references main seller entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`: Belonged seller's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers).
- `event_type`
  > Event type (registered, updated, verified, onboarding_step, suspended,
  > withdrawn, etc).
- `old_value_json`
  > Serialized JSON for previous seller entity state or changed fields
  > (before event).
- `new_value_json`
  > Serialized JSON for new seller entity state or changed fields (after
  > event).
- `triggered_by`: Event initiator (seller, admin, system, integration, etc).
- `meta_json`: Additional event context (IP, device, evidence, linked record, etc).
- `occurred_at`: Datetime when event occurred.
- `created_at`: History record creation datetime.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins`

Administrator accounts for the shoppingMallAiBackend platform. Contains
system operator credentials, profile, and status/state (e.g., super
admin, operator, auditor). Enables permission, system events, and
compliance management. No denormalization/calculated fields. Linked to
admin history events/audit logs.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `email`: Admin's unique business email for system login.
- `password_hash`: Hashed admin password for secure authentication.
- `name`: Full name of the admin for logs and display purposes.
- `role`: Role or access grade for admin (super_admin, operator, auditor, etc).
- `status`: Account status for admin (active, suspended, locked, resigned).
- `joined_at`: Admin joined/registered datetime.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Datetime of last admin attribute update.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion mark timestamp, null if not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_admin_histories`

Historical event/audit records for admin account changes/actions.
Supports full-trail auditing of state/role changes, login attempts,
permission escalations/revocations, and regulatory compliance. Enables
robust accountability and admin activity forensics. Linked to admin
entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Belonged admin's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins).
- `event_type`
  > Type of audit event (created, updated, login, blocked, role_change,
  > password_reset, resigned, etc).
- `meta_json`: Event/context metadata (IP, device, initiator, reason, etc.).
- `occurred_at`: Datetime when event occurred.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when audit record was created.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_products`

Represents the core product entity in the shopping mall platform. Stores
product master data such as name, main attributes, business references,
and maintainable states. Relates to product options, bundles, tags, and
category/channel mappings. Serves as the parent entity for product
snapshots and evidentiary state tracking. Fully normalized for business
data integrity and extensibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `seller_id`
  > Belonged seller's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers). Links
  > product to its owner seller account.
- `code`
  > Business-level unique product code (SKU, external product sync, etc.).
  > Used to trace products across channels and business operations.
- `name`: Product name for retail display and purchase.
- `description`: Detailed product description for customer presentation and business logic.
- `main_image_uri`: Primary image URI for the product. Used in lists and details.
- `status`
  > Product business status (e.g., draft, pending, approved, published,
  > suspended, discontinued).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the product record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the product record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when the product was soft deleted, if applicable.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_options`

Represents an individual product option (such as size, color, variant,
etc.) associated with a product. Each product can have multiple options.
Option SKUs and differentiators are represented here. Linked to product
for parent-child integrity and to option stocks for availability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > The parent product [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products) that this
  > option belongs to.
- `sku`
  > Unique SKU code for this option (might differ from product code for
  > inventory).
- `option_name`: Name describing this option (for example: 'Large', 'Red', '128GB').
- `option_values`
  > Delimited string or JSON representing the values (for multivariate
  > options--for developer parsing and processing).
- `extra_price`
  > Extra price (incremental compared to the main product price) for this
  > option. Used for complex option pricing.
- `main_image_uri`: Representative image URI for this option.
- `status`
  > Business status of this option (active, inactive, discontinued, hidden,
  > etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp this option was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when the option was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for this option if applicable.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_option_stocks`

Represents stock and inventory management for each product option. Tracks
available count, reservation, and warehouse/inbound attributes.
Optionally connected to restock alerts and batch records externally.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_option_id`
  > Linked option [shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_options.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_options) whose
  > stock this record describes.
- `stock_count`: Current available stock of this option.
- `safety_stock`: Configured safety stock value for restocking alerts or business rules.
- `inbound_count`: Quantity on inbound delivery--future stock to be added soon.
- `warehouse_location`: Location or bin/shelf code of this stock in warehouse.
- `status`
  > Stock record's business status (active, reserved, locked, depleted,
  > fragile, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when stock record was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp if this stock record is obsolete.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_snapshots`

Entity preserving full snapshot of a product's state (for auditing,
rollback, compliance, and dispute resolution purposes). Stores all
mutable product business fields at point-in-time. Linked to a specific
product as temporal evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > The product whose state this snapshot records. {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id}
- `snapshot_code`
  > Unique business identifier or code for this snapshot version. Used for
  > evidentiary trace and rollback.
- `snapshot_type`
  > Reason or trigger case for snapshot creation (created, published,
  > modified, price_changed, etc.).
- `name`: Name field of the product at the time of snapshot.
- `description`: Product's main description at this snapshot.
- `main_image_uri`: Product image URI at this snapshot time.
- `status`: Status of product at snapshot time.
- `created_at`: Point-in-time for when the snapshot record was created.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_category_map`

Junction (M:N) table mapping products to categories. For each mapping,
there is a record indicating that a product is classified under a
specific category tree. Category table is external. Used for filtering,
browsing, and category roll-up. Supports denormalized search if needed
via materialized views (not here).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: The referenced product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products).
- `category_id`
  > The category's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_categories) indicating
  > product membership.
- `primary`
  > Indicates whether this is the primary category for this product (vs
  > additional/category roll-ups).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_channel_map`

Junction (M:N) mapping table between products and sales channels.
Associates each product to its available channels (online, offline, B2B,
etc.; channel table is external). Used for channel-based filtering,
access control, and exposure. Can be expanded for channel-specific
overrides (policy, price, etc.).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > Product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products) being mapped to a
  > channel.
- `channel_id`: The sales channel's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_channels).
- `status`
  > Product's business status in this channel mapping (active, inactive,
  > hidden, etc.).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_tags`

Maps products to textual tags for filtering, search, recommendation, and
AI-based personalization logic. Each record links a product to a specific
tag value. Enables rapid AI-based filtering, related product discovery,
and user journey optimization.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: Tagged product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products).
- `tag`
  > The tag string attached to this product (business/AI/search, e.g.
  > 'Eco-Friendly', 'HOT', '소년', etc.).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_search_keywords`

Product-associated search keyword registry. Optimizes search relevance
and recommendation for both business and AI workloads. Supports multiple
search terms for a single product. Used by auto-completion, search logs,
and analytics.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`
  > Product for which this keyword is registered. {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id}
- `search_keyword`
  > Textual keyword that is relevant for business or user-oriented search
  > (e.g. '티셔츠', '패션', '여름옷').

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_bundles`

Represents definition of a product bundle (a set of products sold/managed
together). Each bundle record refers to the master product, and includes
business rules, naming, price overrides, and component breakdown. Used
for bundle pricing, stock, and exposure. Components are mapped in
sub-tables not present here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `main_product_id`: Bundle's master/main product. [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products)
- `code`
  > Unique business code for this product bundle (for business lookup,
  > inventory, or marketing tracing).
- `name`: Human-readable name for the bundle.
- `description`: Bundle description for business and marketing use.
- `bundle_policy`: Bundle policy (manual, auto, campaign-based, etc.).
- `bundle_price`
  > Special pricing for bundle as a unit (can differ from sum of product
  > component prices).
- `status`
  > Business status for bundle record (active, discontinued, hidden,
  > published, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when bundle was created.
- `updated_at`: When the bundle record was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for the bundle record if inactive.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_contents`

Associates products with content sections (images, details, videos,
marketing, etc) by type and business context for rich product display,
localized marketing, AI-based analysis, and operational context. Stores
content type, content URI, order, status, and structured description for
extensibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `product_id`: The referenced product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products).
- `content_type`
  > Type of content (main_image, gallery_image, thumbnail, video, marketing,
  > spec, notice, legal, etc.).
- `content_uri`: URI of the content asset (image, video, or downloadable file location).
- `content_order`: Display sequence/order for this content within product listing/block.
- `content_description`: Textual description or alt text for this content asset.
- `status`: Status of the content section (active, inactive, pending, hidden, etc.).
- `created_at`: Timestamp content record was created.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for content record.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for the content record if no longer needed.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders`

Represents finalized customer orders, the central entity for all
transaction records. Stores references to the customer, order group, and
manages core order-level information such as order number, current
status, total amount, and audit timestamps. All business logic is handled
via related state tables, no calculated fields. Linked to items,
payments, statuses, and snapshots. Provides full compliance trail for
transaction integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers). Links
  > this order to the customer placing it.
- `order_group_id`
  > Order group's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_groups.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_groups).
  > Associates this order to a possible group batch or multichannel grouping.
  > Nullable for stand-alone orders.
- `order_number`
  > Unique business order number for external interface, invoice, or
  > reconciliation. Human-readable, can contain alphanumeric codes.
- `current_status`
  > Current business status of the order (e.g., 'created', 'pending', 'paid',
  > 'cancelled', etc). Must match allowed order workflow states as per
  > business logic.
- `total_amount`
  > Total monetary value of the order, system-calculated by services, stored
  > for audit trace only, never pre-calculated in this schema.
- `currency_code`
  > The ISO currency code (e.g., 'KRW', 'USD'), enables multicurrency
  > support, must match system currency list.
- `note`
  > Business or system note, comment, or explanation for this order, used for
  > internal audit or compliance. Optional.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the order record (immutable).
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp (system-maintained).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp, null if active. Used for business traceability
  > and compliance.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_items`

Line items belonging to each order, representing individual product
purchases. Each item records the product, order reference, unit price,
quantity, and workflow audit. No redundant product info (refer to
snapshot if state matters). Supports complete traceability and compliance
evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > Belonged order's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders). The parent
  > order this line item belongs to.
- `product_id`
  > Referenced product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products). The
  > product being purchased in this line.
- `product_snapshot_id`
  > Referenced product snapshot's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_snapshots.id}. Snapshot at the point of
  > purchase, for historical accuracy.
- `quantity`: Number of product units ordered in this line item.
- `unit_price`: Unit price at purchase time, taken from snapshot, not system-calculated.
- `currency_code`: Currency code at order time (e.g., 'KRW').
- `note`: Item-specific business or system note for audit or workflow.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of order item record.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for audit trail.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp, null if not deleted/active.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_groups`

Order group batches enabling multi-order management such as batch
settlement, partner integration, or multichannel grouping. Used for
combined operations on multiple orders. Links to individual orders as a
foreign key. Captures context, metadata, and unified processing
parameters. Compliance requires full lifecycle audit and traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `group_name`
  > Name or label for the order group for business context (batch job,
  > partner, or channel).
- `external_reference`
  > Reference to external partner/batch process, integrations, or settlement
  > cycles. Optional, nullable.
- `meta_info`
  > Additional business meta data or JSON-encoded information for
  > partner/automation needs (for extensibility).
- `created_at`: Order group creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last group modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for compliance tracking, null if active.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_status_histories`

Immutable history records of all status changes and workflow steps for
each order. Enables full compliance, audit, and process monitoring. Each
entry records from/to state, action trigger, responsible actor
(user/system), audit event context, and precise timestamp. No deletes or
updates allowed (immutable data for evidence).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > Belonged order's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders). Relates each
  > status change record to its parent order.
- `previous_status`
  > Order's business status before the current workflow change (e.g.,
  > 'created', 'pending').
- `new_status`
  > Order's business status after the operation (e.g., 'paid', 'shipped',
  > etc).
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who changed the status (e.g., 'customer', 'seller',
  > 'system', 'admin').
- `actor_id`
  > Reference to the actor (user, system process, etc) who performed the
  > action. References id in the relevant actor table.
- `event_context`
  > Context or note for this workflow event for audit trail (e.g.,
  > 'auto-cancel', 'manual update', 'payment verification').
- `occurred_at`: Timestamp for when the workflow change was executed.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_snapshots`

Archive of full historical state for entire order at the time of any
major business event. Enables rollback, evidence, and compliance.
Snapshots store all order attributes and associated 'frozen' data for
full forensics. Required for audit and legal obligations in e-commerce.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > Belonged order's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders). The order
  > being snapshotted.
- `snapshot_json`
  > Serialized JSON payload of the complete order state, including all
  > contextually relevant business fields at time of snapshot.
- `snapshot_reason`
  > Short text describing the reason for the snapshot (created, confirmed,
  > payment, shipped, etc).
- `created_at`: Date and time the snapshot was taken.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts`

Active or past shopping carts for customers, used for collecting order
candidates and performing session-based purchases. Each cart is owned by
a customer, has created/updated/deleted history for full lifecycle trace
and audit compliance. No denormalized data, products referenced via
cart_items, not here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Referenced customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
  > Links this cart to its owner, can be a member or guest-associated if
  > domain supports guest checkout.
- `session_token`
  > Session or device identifier for unauthenticated users or cross-device
  > linking for guest carts. Optional.
- `status`: Cart business status (e.g., 'active', 'checked_out', 'abandoned', etc.).
- `created_at`: Cart creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp for cart data.
- `deleted_at`: Cart soft deletion date for compliance/lifecycle/state tracking.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_items`

Line items within a shopping cart, each referencing a specific product or
option at selection time. No product data is denormalized; all business
data must reference products table and related snapshot. Used for
accurate checkout, price, and availability confirmation. Soft deletion
enables audit of silent removals.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `cart_id`
  > Parent cart's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts). The cart this
  > line item belongs to.
- `product_id`
  > Referenced product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products). The
  > product being reserved via this cart line.
- `product_option_id`
  > Referenced product option's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_options.id}. Option for the specific
  > variant; nullable if not applicable.
- `quantity`: Qty of product/option selected within the cart item at selection.
- `unit_price`
  > Current price at selection, system-sourced (for checkout
  > confirmation/audit).
- `currency_code`: Currency code used at selection (for multi-currency support in the cart).
- `note`: Business or system note, special requests, temporary flags, etc. Optional.
- `created_at`: Datetime when item was added to cart.
- `updated_at`: Datetime last updated for this item (qty, option, etc).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp when item was removed or invalidated; traceable for
  > audit.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_cart_snapshots`

Historical records of the entire cart state at the time of checkout,
save, removal, or business event trigger. Enables full forensic trace of
'what was in the cart' at any business action time. Designed for audit,
rollback, and compliance with legal retention/evidence rules.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `cart_id`
  > Cart's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_carts). The cart being
  > snapshotted for this compliance record.
- `snapshot_json`
  > Serialized JSON of the cart state (items, quantities, each option, and
  > relevant customer/session context). Only for evidence use, no business
  > logic.
- `snapshot_reason`
  > Reason for cart snapshot (e.g., 'checkout', 'timeout', 'manual',
  > 'failure', etc).
- `created_at`: Timestamp the snapshot was taken.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payments`

Records individual payment attempts/authorizations for each
order—critical for systems with partial, failed, or multiple payment
scenarios. Each payment record has a reference to the parent order, the
payment provider, method, transaction id, result, and important audit
fields. Full compliance with payment and financial audit standards.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_id`
  > Order's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_orders). Which order does this
  > payment instance relate to?
- `payment_provider_id`
  > Payment provider's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_settings.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_settings).
  > Refers to the settings/configuration of payment provider or gateway used
  > for this transaction.
- `payment_method`: Payment method or channel used (card, bank_transfer, mobile, etc).
- `transaction_id`
  > Acquirer or payment gateway transaction/reference id. (For
  > reconciliation, evidence, external audit.)
- `amount`
  > Payment amount for this attempt (system-calculated during workflow, must
  > match order/group rules).
- `currency_code`: ISO currency code of this payment event.
- `payment_result`
  > Result status for this payment event (e.g., 'pending', 'completed',
  > 'failed', 'cancelled').
- `payment_context`
  > Serialized JSON detailing transaction context, metadata, error info, etc.
  > Optional for extensibility.
- `created_at`: Timestamp of payment attempt creation.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp for this payment event.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion timestamp for failed/payments no longer relevant; traceable
  > for audit.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payment_logs`

Finest-grain log for payment processes at each attempt, result, failure,
or integration stage. Captures technical and business audit trail for all
payment interactions, required for payment industry compliance and
security reporting. Relates to the payment record (over multiple logs per
payment); stores request/response, error details, trace context,
timestamps. Not soft deleted due to immutability requirements.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `order_payment_id`
  > Order payment's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payments.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_payments). The
  > payment this log entry is about.
- `log_type`: Type of payment log (e.g., 'request', 'response', 'error', 'event').
- `log_context`
  > Serialized context (e.g., request/response JSON, error stack). Extensible
  > for partner or compliance usage.
- `occurred_at`
  > Precise timestamp log was written. Used for reconciliation and forensic
  > traceability.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_templates`

Coupon template master table, representing the definition and ruleset of
each unique coupon type, including codes, business rule, period,
issuance, and constraint logic. Linked to issued coupons and coupon
histories. Provides the basis for all coupon issuances.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `code`
  > Business unique code for the coupon template. Used for lookup and
  > business integration.
- `name`: Human-readable name of the coupon template for marketing or admin UIs.
- `description`
  > Full description and explanation of the coupon's rules, eligibility, and
  > business context.
- `type`
  > Type of coupon (e.g. discount, free shipping, gift, etc). Specific values
  > documented by business policy.
- `discount_amount`
  > Discount value to be applied by this coupon template. Only raw value, not
  > a calculated field.
- `discount_percent`
  > Percentage based discount (if applicable). Nullable for fixed-amount
  > coupons.
- `min_purchase_amount`
  > Minimum purchase amount required to apply this coupon. Null if not
  > applicable.
- `valid_from`
  > Start datetime for coupon template validity. Controls when coupons can be
  > issued from this template.
- `valid_until`: End datetime for coupon template validity.
- `max_issue_count`
  > Maximum number of coupons that can be issued from this template. Used for
  > event/limited coupons.
- `is_active`
  > Whether this coupon template is currently enabled and open for
  > issuance/use.
- `created_at`: Datetime the coupon template was created in the system.
- `updated_at`: Datetime the coupon template was last updated.
- `deleted_at`
  > Datetime the coupon template was deleted (soft delete). Nullable for
  > active/non-deleted templates.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_issued_coupons`

Issued coupons assigned to individual customers, created based on coupon
templates and issued through marketing, events, or customer actions. One
record per issued coupon. Includes linkage to both the owning customer
and referenced coupon template.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `coupon_template_id`
  > Referenced coupon template's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_templates.id}. Connects issued coupon to
  > template definition.
- `customer_id`
  > Coupon owner's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers). Connects
  > issued coupon to customer entity.
- `code`
  > Unique code for this specific issued coupon, to be used on redemption.
  > Can be different than the template code.
- `issued_at`: Datetime when the coupon was issued to the customer.
- `expires_at`
  > Datetime when this individual coupon expires. Can be within or before
  > template timeframe.
- `used_at`: Datetime when the coupon was actually used. Nullable for unused coupons.
- `status`
  > Lifecycle state of the issued coupon (e.g. issued, used, expired,
  > cancelled). Used for business process tracking.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of the issued coupon record.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp of the issued coupon record.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp for the issued coupon record. Nullable for valid
  > ones.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_histories`

Coupon event and audit trail table. Tracks all significant business
changes and state transitions for coupons (issued, used, expired,
cancelled, etc). Used for audits and business analytics. Stores
references to the issued coupon, actor (who changed status), and the
action metadata.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `issued_coupon_id`
  > Reference to the associated issued coupon's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_issued_coupons.id} for tracking which individual
  > coupon this event refers to.
- `actor_id`
  > Who performed the action (customer/admin/seller) {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id} or {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id}. Identify role context in
  > 'actor_type' field.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who performed the action (e.g. customer, admin, seller).
  > Required to resolve 'actor_id' foreign key target type.
- `action`
  > Business event performed on the coupon (issued, used, expire, cancel,
  > system, etc).
- `action_at`: Datetime the action occurred.
- `remarks`
  > Optional detail or note about this business event for audits or business
  > intelligence.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp of the coupon_history record.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_snapshots`

Snapshot of key business state for each issued coupon. Used for
historical audit, analysis, and state restoration. Contains denormalized
snapshot fields from the issued coupon and related template at point in
time. Immutable after write.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `issued_coupon_id`
  > Snapshot for issued coupon's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_issued_coupons.id} at a specific point in time.
- `coupon_template_code`
  > Coupon template code at time of snapshot. Denormalized for historical
  > accuracy.
- `issued_coupon_code`: The issued coupon's code as of this snapshot.
- `customer_id`
  > Coupon assigned customer's ID. Kept as static value (not FK) for
  > point-in-time reference.
- `status`: Coupon status as of this snapshot (issued, used, etc).
- `valid_from`: Coupon begin validity window (from template or override) at snapshot.
- `valid_until`: Coupon end validity at the snapshot moment.
- `action`: Business event reflected by this snapshot (issued, updated, cancel, etc).
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation datetime.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coupon_usages`

Actual coupon usage records linking issued coupons to orders/products
where they were redeemed. Tracks which order and customer consumed the
coupon and precise usage event for audit, analytics, and revenue
recognition.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `issued_coupon_id`
  > The issued coupon that was used, referencing {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_issued_coupons.id}.
- `order_id`
  > Reference to the redeemed order's {@link

- `created_at`: Creation timestamp for the coupon usage record.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_points`

Point/mileage wallet master record per customer. Aggregates each
customer's mileage/points for event/reward/redemption. One current row
per customer; all mutations tracked by point_histories. Independent of
coupons, but part of the incentives domain.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`

  > value for integrity.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_point_histories`

Full historical log of all point/mileage changes per customer. Ensures
auditability, restores balances, tracks
accruals/redemptions/expiration/corrections. Each record references
parent wallet and can refer to the business event (e.g. order_id,
coupon_id, admin, etc).

- `actor_type`: Who performed the point event (customer, admin, system).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets`

Coin wallet account for holding and transferring virtual coins. Each
wallet is uniquely associated with a customer, seller, or admin via
foreign keys to existing tables, representing the ownership of digital
assets within the platform. The wallet tracks the asset type, wallet
status, security credentials, and is fundamental to any financial or
promotional coin movement. Serves as a root for transaction and balance
records. Only raw field data is stored; no real-time balance caching (see
balances and snapshots).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `wallet_owner_customer_id`
  > Related customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers). Used
  > when the wallet belongs to a customer.
- `wallet_owner_seller_id`
  > Related seller's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers). Used when
  > the wallet belongs to a seller.
- `wallet_owner_admin_id`
  > Related admin's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins). Used when the
  > wallet belongs to an admin.
- `wallet_type`
  > Type of coin. (e.g., reward, event, partner, mainnet, etc.) Represents
  > different coin asset classes in the platform.
- `wallet_status`: Status of the coin wallet (active, locked, withdrawn, closed, etc.).
- `wallet_address`
  > Blockchain or internal address representing the unique identifier for the
  > coin wallet. Used for internal or true blockchains.
- `wallet_label`: Human-readable label for the wallet (user's note or admin-assigned).
- `security_code`
  > Optional security code, PIN, or hashed credential related to wallet
  > operation.
- `created_at`: Created time.
- `updated_at`: Updated time.
- `deleted_at`: Deleted time (soft delete pattern).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_transactions`

Transaction ledger for all coin movements involving platform wallets.
Records all inbound/outbound coin flows, with direct reference to
associated wallet, operation type, numeric delta, resultant balance (at
time), and cross-reference IDs (orders, top-ups, redemptions, admin
grants, etc.). Fundamental to financial and compliance audit trail. Not
denormalized. Each row is one atomic movement.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `wallet_id`
  > Related coin wallet's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets).
  > Reference to the wallet involved in this transaction.
- `transaction_type`: Type of transaction (e.g., deposit, withdrawal, reward, correction, etc.).
- `transaction_amount`
  > The amount (positive or negative) for this movement. Always in coin
  > units, not real money.
- `balance_after_transaction`
  > The balance of the wallet immediately after this transaction. Saved for
  > audit, reconciliation, and historical snapshot reference.
- `reference_id`
  > External or internal reference for business traceability (e.g., order
  > number, top-up id, promotion id).
- `transaction_reason`
  > Text explanation of why this transaction happened (free text, business
  > tag, admin memo).
- `created_at`
  > Time the transaction was created (immutable, audit trail, strictly
  > increasing for a wallet).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_balances`

Point-in-time current balance information for each coin wallet,
non-materialized. Strictly one row per wallet per coin asset (enforced by
unique index). Actual balance is re-calculated by replaying
coin_transactions, this entry is the latest agreed/reconciled state for
audit and UI performance. Used to speed up balance views; all
reconciliation/audit is always possible via full transaction history. No
calculated/derived fields, just snapshot value. Full 3NF. Not to be
denormalized or joined with unrelated tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `wallet_id`: Related coin wallet's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets).
- `balance`
  > Current coin wallet amount as of the most recent transaction
  > replay/reconciliation.
- `balance_at`
  > Timestamp this balance was valid (change after last transaction, for
  > audit).
- `created_at`
  > Row creation timestamp (could be same as balance_at if periodic update,
  > else insertion time).
- `updated_at`: Most recent update to this row.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_snapshots`

Full point-in-time snapshot record of a coin wallet state, created at key
moments (e.g., period closure, audit, reconciliation, incident
investigation). Enables forensic, legal, and compliance proof of wallet
state and full historical drill-downs. Each entry holds all key
coin_wallet attributes and current balance. Retains wallet/owner ref and
all main attributes at the time of snapshot. Cannot be updated, only
appended.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `wallet_id`
  > Coin wallet's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_coin_wallets) at the
  > snapshot point.
- `owner_customer_id`
  > Owner customer id at time of snapshot. For owner lookups/biz reporting.
  > References [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
- `owner_seller_id`
  > Owner seller id at time of snapshot. For owner lookups/biz reporting.
  > References [shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_sellers).
- `owner_admin_id`
  > Owner admin id at time of snapshot. For owner lookups/biz reporting.
  > References [shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_admins).
- `wallet_type`: Copy of the wallet_type at the time of snapshot.
- `wallet_status`: Copy of wallet_status at the time of snapshot.
- `wallet_address`: Wallet address at snapshot time for legal traceability.
- `wallet_label`: Wallet label at snapshot time.
- `security_code`: Security info at snapshot time (null if none/removed).
- `snapshot_balance`
  > Coin balance at snapshot creation, explicit value for legal/compliance
  > proof.
- `snapshot_reason`
  > Explanation/reason for snapshot (e.g., routine audit, reconciliation,
  > incident, user request).
- `snapshot_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp (the point in time this snapshot refers to).
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp of snapshot row physical creation (could be same as snapshot_at
  > for real-time audit).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_wallets`

Mileage wallet entity for holding and managing loyalty (point, mileage,
etc.) balances for customers. Represents a distinct program from coin
wallets; not used for true crypto/backed coins, but for internal loyalty
programs. Each wallet is tied to a single customer (mandatory), and
tracks wallet's program, current status, and security constraints. No
direct monetary or blockchain features. All state changes recorded in
mileage transactions table. Separate from coin subsystem for legal and
program clarity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Reference to the owning customer's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id}. One-to-one to a customer, as
  > customers may only have one mileage wallet per program.
- `wallet_program`
  > Mileage or loyalty program type (brand, affiliate, campaign, seasonal,
  > etc.). Used for multi-program, special events, or white-label points.
- `wallet_status`
  > Current wallet status (active, locked, exhausted, closed), for
  > operational handling.
- `wallet_label`: User-facing or admin note for this wallet (optional display).
- `security_code`: PIN or credential for wallet operation, or null if none.
- `created_at`: Created time.
- `updated_at`: Updated time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-deleted (set on logical deletion only).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_transactions`

Transaction ledger for all point and mileage movements related to
mileage_wallets. Logs every increment/decrement, covering all loyalty
business flows: accumulation, redemption, expiration,
reversal/correction, grants, or adjustments. Each log includes numeric
delta, pre/post balance (as of transaction), linked reference id (e.g.,
order, event), free text reason, and full audit trail. Not denormalized,
no computed fields. Fundamental for math consistency, customer
transparency, and partners/brand auditability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `wallet_id`
  > Mileage wallet's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_wallets.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_mileage_wallets), the
  > source of this transaction.
- `transaction_type`
  > Type of mileage operation (accumulate, redeem, expire, correction, grant,
  > etc.).
- `mileage_amount`
  > How many loyalty points/mileage moved this transaction (positive or
  > negative).
- `balance_after_transaction`
  > Wallet balance after this transaction applies. Used for audit and
  > real-time audit closure.
- `reference_id`
  > External/business reference related to operation (order id, promotion id,
  > etc.).
- `transaction_reason`
  > Reason for/change cause for transaction operation, business-side or
  > customer note.
- `created_at`: Transaction creation time (immutable, for audit trail).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries`

Product inquiry entity representing a transactional inquiry or question
made by a customer about a specific product. Stores information such as
title, content, public/private status, customer, product references, and
is tightly coupled with AI moderation, review, and snapshot/audit use
cases. Key for customer-to-seller interactions, with access restrictions
and a full state/audit trail via snapshots and events. Linked to
customers, products, and optionally associated attachments.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`
  > Referencing inquirer customer’s {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id}.
- `product_id`: Referenced product’s [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products).
- `title`: Title of the inquiry. Required. 200 bytes max.
- `body`
  > The main content of the inquiry. Required. Subject to length validations
  > and profanity spam/AI analysis.
- `public`
  > Whether the inquiry is publicly visible. If false, only the inquirer and
  > admin/seller can see it.
- `status`
  > Processing status (e.g., waiting, answered, blocked, under review), for
  > workflow state management.
- `answer_id`: Direct answer reference for 1:1 linkage. Nullable if no answer yet.
- `ai_sentiment_score`: AI sentiment analysis result score (-1.0 negative ~ 1.0 positive).
- `ai_spam_score`: AI-based spam/abuse score. Higher is more likely abuse.
- `created_at`: Creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp (null means active, otherwise deleted).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_reviews`

Product review entity for transactional user/customer feedback (star
rating, comment, optional files/tags) on a purchased product. Used for
reputation, recommendation, and analytics. Links to customer, product;
also processed by AI moderation and subject to audit trail via snapshots.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Review submission customer [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers).
- `product_id`: Reviewed product [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products).
- `order_item_id`
  > Order item to which this review is attached {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_order_items.id}.
- `title`: Title of the review (optional, for display/search purposes).
- `body`: Detailed review content. Subject to AI analysis. Required.
- `rating`: Star rating (e.g., 1-5). Business rules enforce valid range.
- `status`
  > Workflow/status (normal, blocked, deleted, etc.), for moderation and
  > business processing.
- `ai_sentiment_score`: AI-derived sentiment score (-1.0 negative ~ 1.0 positive).
- `ai_spam_score`: AI spam detection/confidence (higher more abnormal).
- `created_at`: Review creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp, null if normal state.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_inquiry_snapshots`

Historical snapshot for each product inquiry as audit evidence. Preserves
the time-specific state of an inquiry (title, body, status, public flag,
AI fields, and actor) at change events. Used for compliance and rollback,
tightly linked to its inquiry. Each change to an inquiry creates a new
snapshot record.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `inquiry_id`
  > Reference to target inquiry {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries.id}.
- `title`: Snapshot: Inquiry title at the snapshot point.
- `body`: Snapshot: Inquiry content at the snapshot point.
- `public`: Snapshot: Whether the inquiry was public at this change.
- `status`: Snapshot: Inquiry workflow status at this change.
- `actor_id`
  > Person (customer, seller, admin) making the change. Stores audit actor
  > [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers) or admin/seller references.
- `ai_sentiment_score`: Snapshot: Sentiment score at this stage.
- `ai_spam_score`: Snapshot: Spam score at this revision.
- `changed_at`: Point in time when this change was made.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_review_snapshots`

Historical snapshot for each product review, preserving review content,
rating, AI values, and workflow status at each change event. Key for
audit/compliance and rollback scenarios, tightly coupled to the review
entity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `review_id`
  > Reference to target review {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_reviews.id}.
- `body`: Snapshot of review text at change point.
- `rating`: Snapshot star rating at this moment.
- `status`: Snapshot workflow/business status.
- `actor_id`
  > Person (customer, seller, admin) doing this change. Reference to
  > customer/admin/seller tables.
- `ai_sentiment_score`: Snapshot: Sentiment score at this moment.
- `ai_spam_score`: Snapshot: Spam score at this revision.
- `changed_at`: Timestamp the snapshot was made.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_moderation_events`

Moderation event audit table. Records all moderation actions (block,
unblock, edit, warn, escalate) for an inquiry or review, with actor,
reason, and linked target entity. Supports AI-driven and manual
moderation, compliance, and historical integrity. Used for dispute and
enforcement workflows.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `target_inquiry_id`
  > Target inquiry, if event applies to an inquiry. Nullable for review-only
  > events. References [shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries).
- `target_review_id`
  > Target review, if event applies to a review. Nullable for inquiry-only
  > events. References [shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_reviews.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_reviews).
- `actor_id`
  > Who performed this event: customer, seller, admin. References
  > customer/seller/admin tables as needed.
- `event_type`
  > Type of moderation (block, unblock, edit, warning, escalate, etc.). For
  > workflow, analytics, and stats.
- `reason`
  > Human/moderator/AI reason/explanation for moderation. Nullable for auto
  > cases.
- `attached_ai_evidence_id`
  > Reference to any AI-generated evidence or report in attachments table.
  > Nullable if manual.
- `referenced_event_id`: Reference to prior event, if this event is corrective/related. Nullable.
- `created_at`: Event creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_appeals`

Appeal or objection entity for inquiry or review moderation
events—created by users (customer, seller) or admin to dispute moderation
results. Contains references to the original moderation event, the
appealor, status, decision, comments, and timestamps. Enables workflow
for appeal, review, and decision tracking, supports compliance and legal
obligation for reconsideration/complaint processing.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `moderation_event_id`
  > Moderation event being appealed {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_moderation_events.id}.
- `appellant_id`
  > Who appeals the event (customer, seller, admin). Refers to appellant in
  > customers, sellers, or admins.
- `status`: Appeal status (pending, approved, rejected, under review, etc.).
- `decision_comment`: Admin’s or moderator's decision note. Nullable until adjudicated.
- `created_at`: Appeal creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last update to appeal record (status, comment changes, etc.).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_products`

Favorite products table. Tracks which products are favorited by which
customers. Each record indicates a single customer favoriting a single
product. Uniquely combines customer and product. For scalability,
extensibility to bundles or product options is possible via additional
FKs. Business use: personalized product recommendations, favorite list,
alerting on restock/discount/news. Each favorite may have a corresponding
snapshot for historical object state preservation. Related to {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers}, {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_products}, and associated
snapshots/notifications.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Favoriting customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers)
- `product_id`: Favorited product's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_products)
- `created_at`: Favorite creation timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft deletion timestamp for unfavorite (null if active, set upon removal).

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_inquiries`

Favorite inquiries table. Tracks product inquiries, reviews, or Q&A that
a customer bookmarks for later reference or notification. Supports unique
per customer/inquiry relation. Used for personalized customer experience
and inquiry alerting. Linked with inquiry table for reference, customer
table, and may have corresponding snapshot for historical content.
Related to [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers), {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Owner customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers)
- `inquiry_id`: Favorited inquiry's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_product_inquiries)
- `created_at`: Favorite creation timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp when favorite was removed.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_addresses`

Favorite addresses table. Allows users to bookmark frequently used
shipping or billing addresses for quick order or delivery selection.
Ensures personalization and efficient address management. References the
customer and their address. Each favorite address is unique per
customer/address combination. Related to {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers}, {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_addresses}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `customer_id`: Owner customer's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_customers)
- `address_id`
  > Bookmarked address's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_customer_addresses.id}
- `created_at`: Timestamp the address was marked as favorite.
- `deleted_at`: Timestamp address was removed from favorites.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_snapshots`

Favorite object snapshots. Historical records of the state of a favorited
object (product, inquiry, or address) at the time it was favorited.
Provides evidence, audit, and rollback for compliance and evidence
management. Each snapshot records the related favorite, the type of
target, the snapshot object ID, and serialized object state. This design
supports multi-object favorites extension. Used for legal proof, audit
trails, and restoration on rollback requests. Related to favorite FK
tables by favorite_id, target typing via enum.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_product_id`
  > Relates to product favorites. Nullable for other types. FK to {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_products.id}
- `favorite_inquiry_id`
  > Relates to inquiry favorites. Nullable for other types. FK to {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_inquiries.id}
- `favorite_address_id`
  > Relates to address favorites. Nullable for other types. FK to {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_addresses.id}
- `target_type`
  > Type indicator for the favorited object at snapshot (e.g., PRODUCT,
  > INQUIRY, ADDRESS).
- `snapshot_object_id`
  > The exact object ID (product/inquiry/address) this snapshot records. Used
  > for audit and recovery.
- `serialized_object`
  > JSON serialized snapshot of the object state (full fields as stringified
  > JSON).
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_notifications`

Notifications for favorite objects. Logs or queues notification events
for favorites (e.g. product restocked, price dropped, new inquiry
response) per user-object. Supports delivery channel, alert type,
read/unread state, link to favorite record. Used for alert history,
redundancy checks, and notification retries. Relates to corresponding
favorite FKs and optionally stores delivery metadata. Designed for future
expansion to various favorite types.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `favorite_product_id`
  > Product favorite related notification. Nullable for non-product events.
  > FK to [shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_products.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_products)
- `favorite_inquiry_id`
  > Inquiry favorite related notification. Nullable for non-inquiry events.
  > FK to [shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_inquiries.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_inquiries)
- `favorite_address_id`
  > Address favorite related notification. Nullable for non-address events.
  > FK to [shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_addresses.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_favorite_addresses)
- `notification_type`
  > Type of notification event (e.g. RESTOCK, PRICE_DROP, INQUIRY_REPLY,
  > ADDRESS_CHANGED).
- `notification_channel`: Delivery channel for the notification (e.g. PUSH, EMAIL, SMS).
- `read`: Whether the notification has been read by the user.
- `delivery_metadata`
  > Additional delivery details or 3rd-party service response data.
  > JSON-serialized. Nullable.
- `created_at`: Notification creation timestamp.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles`

Represents a content article (BBS post, news, FAQ, marketing, or fixed
site content) managed independently of transactional reviews/inquiries.
Each record contains primary article content, metadata (title, summary,
status), attribution (author, type), and references to categories and
optionally pinned status. Designed for board/news systems and independent
content in e-commerce portals. Relates to {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_categories} for content organization and
to [shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_snapshots](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_snapshots) for versioning.
Author is referenced by customer, seller, or admin in other tables.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `category_id`
  > Article's belonged category's {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_categories.id}
- `author_type`
  > Type of author (customer|seller|admin) indicating the entity that created
  > the article. Used to resolve relation in application logic.
- `author_id`
  > Author's UUID from the appropriate reference table, depending on
  > author_type (customer, seller, or admin).
- `title`: Article title or headline. User-visible and indexed for search.
- `summary`
  > Short summary or preview content. Used for listing and SEO/metatag
  > presentation.
- `body`
  > The full article content in HTML or rich text. Main content block for the
  > article.
- `status`
  > Business status code (published|draft|hidden|deleted). Used for state
  > transitions and logical access control.
- `view_count`
  > Total number of views for the article for analytics and popularity.
  > Incremented on read.
- `comment_count`: Current number of comments for the article (not snapshot, updated live).
- `created_at`: Datetime when the article was created.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when the article was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Datetime when the article was soft deleted. Null when not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_categories`

Represents the article categories for organizing articles/posts in
BBS/news/FAQ sections. Supports parent-child nesting for category trees.
Used for grouping, navigation, and filtering. Relates to articles via
[shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles.category_id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `parent_id`
  > Optional parent category for hierarchy. {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_categories.id}.
- `name`: Category name displayed to users.
- `code`: Category business code for internal lookup and integration.
- `sort_order`: Display order among sibling categories for navigation menu.
- `is_active`: Whether this category is active and selectable.
- `created_at`: Datetime when the category was created.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when the category was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Datetime when the category was soft deleted. Null when not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_comments`

Stores comments and replies (threaded comments) for articles. Each
comment is associated with an article and optionally references a parent
comment to support nesting (threaded replies). Includes author
information (UUID reference and type), content, metadata (status, report
count, like count), and temporal/audit fields. Tied to {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles} via foreign key and supports
moderation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `article_id`: Referenced article's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles)
- `parent_id`
  > Optional parent comment for nested (threaded) replies. {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_comments.id}
- `author_type`
  > Type of author (customer|seller|admin) indicating the entity that created
  > the comment.
- `author_id`
  > Author's UUID from the reference table, depending on author_type
  > (customer, seller, or admin).
- `body`: Comment/reply body text.
- `status`
  > Business status (published|hidden|reported|deleted). Used for moderation
  > and logical access control.
- `like_count`: Total number of likes/upvotes on this comment.
- `report_count`
  > Number of reports this comment has received (used for moderation
  > triggers).
- `created_at`: Datetime when the comment was created.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when the comment was last updated.
- `deleted_at`: Datetime when the comment was soft deleted. Null when not deleted.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_pinned`

Represents records for pinned (featured) articles to distinguish
highlighted or promoted content. Used for temporary or permanent
top-of-list display for portal/board sections. Pin duration, status, and
administrative metadata are tracked. Related to {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles} for the pin-article relationship.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `article_id`: The [shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles) that is being pinned.
- `started_at`
  > Datetime when the pin period started. For permanent pins, equals
  > created_at.
- `ended_at`: Datetime when the pin period ended. Null for permanent/active pins.
- `reason`
  > Administrative reason or business context for pinning this article (for
  > moderation/audit reports).
- `created_at`: Datetime when the pin entry was created.
- `updated_at`: Datetime when the pin entry was changed.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_article_snapshots`

Maintains historic snapshots (point-in-time copies) of article records
for full audit trails, legal evidence, and restoration purposes. Each
snapshot is tied to an article and stores all business-critical fields as
they existed at creation time. Enables rollback, auditing, and recovery
for articles. Used for legal, compliance, and business continuity
processes. Links to the article by {@link
shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles.id}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `article_id`
  > The target article's [shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles.id](#shopping_mall_ai_backend_articles) for
  > this snapshot version.
- `title`: Snapshot of article title at snapshot time.
- `summary`: Snapshot of article summary at snapshot time.
- `body`: Snapshot of full article content at snapshot time.
- `author_type`: Type of author (customer|seller|admin) at snapshot time.
- `author_id`: Snapshot value of author's UUID.
- `status`: Business status at the snapshot point.
- `category_id`: Snapshot value for category.
- `pinned_id`: Snapshot value for pinned record if present.
- `view_count`: View count at snapshot time.
- `comment_count`: Comment count at snapshot time.
- `created_at`
  > Datetime when the snapshot version was created (for the article's
  > history/audit).
