### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_compliance_events`

Records of all compliance-related events, including policy changes,
regulatory updates, data subject requests, and system compliance
triggers. Serves as the canonical audit for all compliance actions within
the platform. Each event may reference related entities, users, or logs,
but maintains independence as the system-wide compliance ledger. Used to
drive audit readiness and demonstrate regulatory adherence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `event_type`
  > Type of compliance event (e.g., policy_update, data_erasure_request,
  > access_review). Free-form string for extensibility but typically follows
  > system taxonomy.
- `actor_id`
  > Unique identifier of user, admin, or subsystem that triggered the event.
  > Null if event source is system-initiated with no user attached.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who caused the event (e.g., admin, customer, seller,
  > subsystem). Used for audit traceability.
- `target_type`
  > Type of target entity affected by this event (such as table name or
  > domain object name). Required for event trace context.
- `target_id`
  > Unique identifier of the affected entity for compliance trace. If event
  > is global, this may be null.
- `event_payload`
  > Arbitrary structured payload (JSON string) containing event attributes
  > for compliance proof; may include snapshot of state, change reason, or
  > regulatory data.
- `created_at`
  > Timestamp of event record creation. Used for audit ordering and
  > regulatory timelines.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_compliance_snapshots`

Snapshot records of compliance-critical data at the time of events, such
as data subject requests, erasure, policy state, or system configuration
for regulatory proof and rollback. Provides immutable evidence and
supports forensic investigations or rollback. Each snapshot is associated
with a specific compliance event, and optionally with end-user, product,
or data entity for audit linkage.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `compliance_event_id`
  > Associated compliance event {@link
  > shopping_mall_ai_backend_compliance_events.id} that triggered this
  > snapshot. Required for audit chaining.
- `entity_type`
  > Type of the business/data entity for which the snapshot is preserved
  > (e.g., customer, product, order, admin, system_setting). Required for
  > regulatory traceability.
- `entity_id`
  > Unique identifier of the entity for snapshot evidence. Null if snapshot
  > is global (e.g., system policy).
- `snapshot_payload`
  > Full JSON-formatted snapshot of data for evidence. Immutable record for
  > compliance and rollback.
- `created_at`: Snapshot creation timestamp for audit chain and retention policies.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_business_rules`

Catalog of enforced business rules and regulatory policies in the
platform. Tracks rule code, description, enforcement status, reason for
changes, and timeline of revisions for regulatory audit. Supports system
introspection, helps drive automated compliance checks and provides
business context for historical events.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `rule_code`
  > Unique system code for business rule or regulatory policy (e.g.,
  > GDPR_ART17, ORDER_CANCELLATION_WINDOW). Used for programmatic lookup and
  > system introspection.
- `rule_description`
  > Detailed description and context for the rule; includes legal or business
  > rationale. Used for compliance documentation and system explainability.
- `enforcement_status`
  > Current enforcement status (e.g., active, suspended, retired, draft,
  > obsolete).
- `reason_for_change`
  > Description of why and when the rule/policy was updated, if applicable.
  > Optional; used for compliance trace and version justification.
- `effective_from`
  > Date and time from which the rule or policy took effect for historical
  > reasonability and audit verification.
- `effective_to`: Date/time when the rule was superseded or retired. Null if still active.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp for audit history.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification to rule or policy record.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_access_logs`

System-wide access logs recording each API, admin, customer, or subsystem
access event. Provides a detailed immutable trail of all user and system
accesses for security and compliance. Includes context such as IP
address, user agent, location (when available), and reason codes. Used
for monitoring, anomaly detection, and audit evidence.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `access_type`
  > Type of access event (e.g., login, api_call, file_download, admin_action,
  > token_refresh). Used for compliance audit and risk analytics.
- `actor_id`
  > ID of user, admin, or subsystem responsible for this access. Null if not
  > user-driven.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor who performed the access (admin, customer, seller,
  > subsystem, or integration). For audit and traceability.
- `source_ip`
  > Remote IP address logged for the access event, for forensic trace and
  > security checks.
- `user_agent`
  > User agent string (browser/device/app/environment info) captured at
  > access time.
- `location_label`
  > Location or geo label if available. e.g., 'KR-Seoul', 'US-West',
  > 'Remote'. Used for advanced analytics.
- `access_payload`
  > Raw log payload for dynamic fields and future-regulation compatibility
  > (JSON or free-form).
- `occurred_at`: Time that access event occurred, for precise audit sequencing.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_security_logs`

Logs of all security, anomaly, and threat events throughout the platform,
such as failed logins, suspicious behavior, policy violations, brute
force attempts, or detected vulnerabilities. Designed for regulatory
evidence and proactive security operations. Used by both SecOps and
compliance officers to monitor for security breaches and regulatory
reporting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `event_type`
  > Type of security event (e.g., failed_login, brute_force,
  > policy_violation, api_misuse, vulnerability_detected, system_intrusion).
- `actor_id`
  > Unique ID of relevant user/admin/subsystem responsible. Null if automated
  > system event.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor for traceability (admin, customer, seller, subsystem,
  > automation, external).
- `alert_level`
  > Severity or level of the security incident (info, warning, alert,
  > critical). Enables rapid filtering and escalations.
- `alert_payload`
  > Full context of alert in JSON or free-form. Contains risk analysis
  > result, stack traces, trigger patterns, policy references, etc.
- `occurred_at`: Timestamp of the security event record, for audit timelines.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_system_events`

System-wide event log for significant backend incidents, operational
notifications, process automations, scheduled jobs, or cross-domain
platform triggers of long-term audit value. Essential for
enterprise-scale monitoring, support escalations, and system health
tracking. Designed for compliance and incident response documentation.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `system_event_type`
  > Nature of the system event (deployment, scheduled_job, maintenance,
  > incident, service_restart, config_change, integration_event,
  > data_restore, etc.)
- `summary`
  > Brief summary of the event context or message. Used for system dashboards
  > and alerting.
- `event_payload`
  > Detailed contents/background as JSON or text. Used for investigation and
  > compliance root cause analysis.
- `severity_level`
  > Severity/impact assessment (info, notice, warning, error, critical).
  > Drives escalations and reporting.
- `occurred_at`: When the system event occurred, for audit and incident sequencing.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_error_logs`

Platform error and exception logs capturing business errors, integration
failures, external API faults, and unexpected exceptions. Facilitates
debugging and is required for incident management, SRE, and compliance
reporting for critical outages. Must support rich search and complete
root cause data for regulatory transparency.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `error_code`
  > Application-unique code for error classification. Used for systematic
  > troubleshooting and regulatory reporting.
- `error_message`: Short summary/label of the error or exception for operator awareness.
- `error_context`
  > Detailed error context (e.g., stacktrace, input, affected entity). Stores
  > root cause information in JSON or plain text.
- `root_cause_entity_type`
  > Affected business/system entity type for error traceability (e.g., order,
  > product, user, payment, subsystem).
- `root_cause_entity_id`
  > Unique ID of the direct entity involved in the error. Null if not
  > applicable (e.g., system error).
- `severity_level`
  > Operational impact of the error (info, warning, error, critical, fatal).
  > For SRE and compliance reporting.
- `occurred_at`: When the error was captured, for audit trace and incident reconstruction.

### `shopping_mall_ai_backend_audit_logs`

Comprehensive audit log capturing all key business, administrative,
policy, and user/account actions for the platform. Each entry records
critical who/what/when/why context to support compliance reporting and
legal defensibility. Used for end-to-end monitoring, forensic
investigations, and regulatory disclosures. The central ledger for system
integrity.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `action_type`
  > Type of action performed (e.g., create, update, delete, access, export,
  > review, policy_amendment, approval, rejection, unlock, error...).
- `actor_id`
  > User, admin, or subsystem UUID responsible for the action. Can be null if
  > performed automatically by system.
- `actor_type`
  > Category of actor responsible (admin, customer, seller, subsystem,
  > automation).
- `target_type`
  > Type of the target business entity involved in the audited action (e.g.,
  > user, product, policy, rule, settings, etc).
- `target_id`
  > UUID of the target entity for precise linkage. Null if no specific entity
  > (global/system actions).
- `description`
  > Human-readable description giving full audit context, rationale, and
  > supporting remarks for compliance reviewers.
- `audit_payload`
  > Detailed payload (JSON or text) capturing state, before/after info, or
  > regulatory attachment. Used for root-cause audit trail.
- `occurred_at`: Time that the action/audit event took place for timeline and integrity.
